newsitem.title: CANADA: PRESS DIGEST - Canada - Thursday, July 17, 1997.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Canada - Thursday, July 17, 1997.

text.p: The following are top headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-Annan vows UN 'revolution:' Administrative overhaul would give him deputy and 4-member 'cabinet'
-Clark withdraws B.C. labour bill: Massive pressure from business groups forces NDP government to back down
-Versace a homebody in a fast crowd: As a manhunt continues in Miami's gay clubs, police get information that may help nab killer.
-Sailors trapped in legal doldrums: Maersk Dubai's Filipino crewman have been confused and demoralized by a seemingly endless round of hearings and court appearances.
-Dow surges past 8,000: Encouraged by robust earnings, low interest rates, investors send markets to record highs
-Avenor to sell Pacific Forest stake to TimberWest: Deal to create largest timberland owner in B.C.
-Oppenheimer seen costing $500-million: CIBC said to be close to a deal
-B of M asks Ottawa to lift ban on Big Six mergers
-Avenor plans B.C. selloff: Further reshaping the landscape of the troubled B.C. forestry sector, the Montreal-based firm isselling stake in Pacific Forest to TimberWest
-Bank of Montreal urges Ottawa to tear down barriers in financial services
